macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: European stocks edge higher as oil falls and Nvidia earnings loom
items.summary: European shares rose modestly, with the STOXX 600 up 0.1%, as lower oil prices eased bond yields and investors awaited Nvidia’s results for clues on AI demand. Reuters noted basic resources led gains, while broader risk sentiment improved on hopes of a reopening in the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Global markets firmer as oil retreat lifts bonds and softens inflation concerns
items.summary: Stocks advanced across major regions, with the S&P 500 up 0.3%, Nasdaq 100 up 0.6%, and Dow Jones up 0.3% as oil prices fell and Treasury yields declined. Reuters/Bloomberg reporting said Brent and WTI dropped sharply, the 10-year Treasury yield fell to 4.63%, and traders looked ahead to Nvidia earnings and U.S. inflation data.

items.title: Dollar eases as Treasury buybacks and Iran-related headlines support risk assets
items.summary: The U.S. dollar index slipped 0.07% to 98.92 while the euro edged higher to $1.1673. Market coverage linked the move to lower Treasury yields, Treasury buyback activity, and easing inflation pressure from softer oil prices.

items.title: Fed-sensitive data in focus as traders await U.S. GDP, PCE, and durable goods
items.summary: Markets are watching upcoming U.S. GDP, personal spending, core PCE, and durable goods orders for clues on the Federal Reserve’s policy path. Several market briefings highlighted that softer oil and lower yields have reduced inflation concerns, while gold remained near a multi-month high.

items.title: Nvidia earnings are the key event for global equities
items.summary: Multiple market briefings flagged Nvidia’s upcoming earnings as the main stock-market catalyst of the day, with investors seeking confirmation that AI demand remains strong. Futures were mildly mixed in early trading, with U.S. equity futures slightly lower and European futures pointing to a firmer open.

items.title: Asian and Indian markets steady to higher on easing crude prices
items.summary: Asian risk sentiment improved as oil slid and inflation fears receded, while Indian benchmarks also closed higher. The Nifty 50 gained 116 points to 24,335 and the Sensex added 287 points to 77,656.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin briefly tops $81K before retreating; broader crypto market pulls back
items.summary: Bitcoin hit a high near $81.2K in the past 24 hours before easing back to around $78.9K, while total crypto market capitalization slipped from about $2.71 trillion to $2.65 trillion. Several major coins, including ETH, XRP, and SOL, also traded lower on the day.

items.title: Crypto market turns lower as major altcoins fall 2% to 5%
items.summary: A market recap reported Bitcoin losing the $80,000 level and Ethereum, Binance Coin, and Ripple declining by roughly 2% to 5%. The move was framed as a broad retreat after recent gains.

items.title: Japan reportedly weighing lower crypto taxes and easier stablecoin rules
items.summary: Reports say Japan is considering a uniform 20% crypto tax rate and also easing stablecoin restrictions to allow use in large-value payments such as automobiles and real estate. The policy shift would be a notable regulatory development for the local market if enacted.

items.title: European authorities seize $1.51B bitcoin-mixing service Cryptomixer
items.summary: European authorities reportedly seized a bitcoin-mixing service tied to about $1.51 billion in transactions. The action underscores continued enforcement pressure on crypto privacy and laundering tools.

items.title: Ethereum developers prepare Fusaka upgrade; network roadmap advances
items.summary: Ethereum developers are preparing the Fusaka upgrade, described as the second major Ethereum upgrade of 2025. The news highlights continued protocol work on scaling and network improvements.

items.title: Monad mainnet launch goes live
items.summary: CoinDesk’s protocol roundup highlighted Monad’s blockchain going live, alongside an airdrop. The launch adds another notable project development to the day’s crypto news cycle.

items.title: Russia’s digital ruble adoption expands to telecom and e-commerce payments
items.summary: A report said Russian telecom operators and e-commerce platforms will begin accepting digital ruble payments starting in September. That would mark a meaningful step in CBDC adoption if implemented as described.

items.title: India expected to issue first tokenized corporate bond in September
items.summary: Market reporting says India plans to issue its first tokenized corporate bond next month. The development would be a significant milestone for real-world asset tokenization in the country.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI’s Jalapeño chip benchmark results surface
items.summary: OpenAI reported that its in-house Jalapeño inference chip delivered 1.5x-1.9x more AI work per watt and 1.7x-3.6x lower latency than Nvidia chips across several benchmark workloads. The announcement adds to the broader industry trend toward custom silicon for AI inference.

items.title: Apple unveils new Mac mini and Mac Studio focused on AI performance
items.summary: Apple introduced updated Mac mini and Mac Studio desktops, emphasizing faster AI performance and positioning them for developers and AI-heavy workloads. The company also highlighted improvements in graphics, storage, and connectivity.

items.title: Skild AI debuts S1 robotics foundation model
items.summary: Skild AI announced S1, a robotics foundation model that it says can learn tasks never seen during pretraining from a single video demo without fine-tuning. The release reflects growing momentum around general-purpose embodied AI and robotics models.

items.title: OpenAI data center leadership turnover continues
items.summary: OpenAI confirmed that Chris Malone, its former head of data centers, has left the company. His departure comes amid broader executive changes as OpenAI expands its compute infrastructure.

items.title: Perplexity launches a local version of Perplexity Computer
items.summary: Perplexity rolled out Portable Computer, a fully local version of Perplexity Computer that supports Qwen3.8-27B and Perplexity’s PPLX 27B on Nvidia DGX Spark hardware. The move points to rising demand for on-device and local AI workflows.

items.title: IBM Research announces Granite 4.2
items.summary: IBM Research introduced Granite 4.2, a model family focused on agentic reasoning and speech, with 3B, 8B, and 30B versions posted on Hugging Face. The release underscores continued competition in specialized enterprise AI models.

items.title: Google Cloud launches Gemini Enterprise packages for legal and financial services
items.summary: Google Cloud unveiled Gemini Enterprise for Legal and Gemini Enterprise for Financial Services, signaling a push toward industry-specific AI products. The announcements fit a broader trend of vendors packaging general models into regulated-sector solutions.

items.title: OpenAI Assistants API reaches end-of-life
items.summary: OpenAI’s Assistants API was formally discontinued, prompting developer migration to newer tooling and workflows. The shutdown is part of OpenAI’s broader platform consolidation.

items.title: XPENG robotics business raises over $900 million
items.summary: XPENG’s robotics arm reportedly raised more than $900 million in its first funding round, marking one of the largest humanoid-robotics financings in China. The deal highlights investor appetite for embodied AI and robotics.

items.title: AI industry shift toward inference accelerates
items.summary: A roundup of the past 24 hours described the AI sector as shifting from training to inference, citing mass production of inference-focused accelerators and new work on accountability systems for AI agents. This reflects a broader industry emphasis on deployment efficiency and operational governance.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Gamescom Opening Night Live 2026 delivered a flood of major game reveals
items.summary: Multiple outlets reported that the Gamescom showcase featured roughly 55 announcements and trailers, including new looks at Gears of War: E-Day, Final Fantasy 7 Revelations, and several surprise reveals. Coverage also highlighted remasters, sequels, and release-date updates across PC and console platforms.

items.title: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered announced as a free upgrade
items.summary: CD Projekt announced a remastered version of The Witcher 3 with improved visuals, rendering, movement, combat, and animations. Several reports say it will arrive on September 29, 2026 as a free upgrade for existing owners on compatible platforms.

items.title: Control Resonant gets a release date
items.summary: Coverage of Gamescom Opening Night Live says Remedy's Control Resonant is set to launch on September 24, 2026. Reports list PS5, Xbox Series X/S, Steam, Epic Games Store, and GeForce NOW as launch platforms, with Mac support coming later.

items.title: AION 2 announced for global release in October
items.summary: NCSOFT used Gamescom to confirm that AION 2 will launch globally on October 5, 2026. Coverage notes the MMORPG will arrive on PC and that the date is slightly later than initially expected.

items.title: Gears of War: E-Day shows new story footage and a release window
items.summary: Xbox showcased a new story trailer for Gears of War: E-Day during the event, giving a fresh look at the prequel's narrative. Reports also mention an October 6, 2026 release for Xbox.

items.title: Turok: Origins delayed to spring 2027
items.summary: Saber Interactive reportedly pushed Turok: Origins out of its original fall 2026 window. Multiple coverage roundups say the game is now scheduled for spring 2027 across PS5, Xbox Series X/S, Nintendo Switch 2, and PC.

items.title: Path of Exile 2 leaves Early Access in December
items.summary: Gamescom coverage says Path of Exile 2 version 1.0 will launch on December 11, 2026 and transition the game to free-to-play. The update is also said to add swords as a new weapon type.

items.title: Heroes of Might and Magic III Remake announced
items.summary: Ubisoft reportedly unveiled a remake of Heroes of Might and Magic III, including content from the original game's two expansions. The announcement did not include a release date.

items.title: Mewgenics is coming to consoles
items.summary: Coverage says Mewgenics will launch on PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and Switch 2 on September 8, 2026 after its earlier PC release. The game was among the notable announcements from the Gamescom showcase.

items.title: Helldivers 2 adds the Force of Law Warbond
items.summary: Earlier gaming-news coverage reported that Helldivers 2 is getting a new Force of Law Warbond. The announcement expands the cooperative shooter with fresh unlocks for players.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Apple refreshes Mac mini and Mac Studio with new chips
items.summary: Apple unveiled updated Mac mini and Mac Studio models, including the Mac mini with M6 and M5 Pro chips, alongside faster storage, graphics, and connectivity. The launch is one of the biggest non-AI consumer hardware announcements in the past day.

items.title: Amazon says Mechanical Turk will shut down in September 2026
items.summary: AWS plans to discontinue Mechanical Turk on September 30, 2026, ending the 21-year-old crowdsourced task platform. The move marks a notable change for one of Amazon’s longest-running internet services.

items.title: WhatsApp upgrades two-step verification and passkey support
items.summary: WhatsApp rolled out a stronger two-step verification option that lets users replace the six-digit PIN with a longer alphanumeric password. It also added support for multiple passkeys, expanding account security features.

items.title: Uber adds live ride tracking for parents of teen riders
items.summary: Uber launched an optional safety feature that lets parents or guardians watch a livestream of their teen’s ride through the driver’s front-facing phone camera. The feature is aimed at improving visibility and safety for family accounts.

items.title: Taiwan charges nine over illegal AI server exports to China
items.summary: Taiwanese prosecutors charged nine people, including staff linked to Nvidia and Super Micro, over alleged illegal exports of high-end servers to China. The case highlights continuing trade and export-control scrutiny around advanced hardware.

items.title: Australia bans AI-generated tracks from official music charts
items.summary: Australia’s recorded music industry said tracks wholly generated by AI will be barred from official charts. The policy is a significant non-software tech-industry response to generative tools affecting creative markets.

items.title: Nvidia unveils Jetson Orin Nano 2 edge computer
items.summary: Nvidia introduced the Jetson Orin Nano 2 edge AI computer, saying it doubles inference performance and offers 78 TOPS of AI compute. While AI-related, it is primarily a hardware product launch rather than a model announcement.
